conflicts.issue: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws, Law Enforcement Role, and Inter-Board Process
conflicts.summary: City and County elected officials clashed sharply over the proposed 24-month Community Safety and Wellness Task Force—dividing over whether it delayed urgent anti-violence action, whether law enforcement should be excluded from voting membership, and whether the rollout respected county partners.
conflicts.side_a_position: Advance a 24-month community-driven task force without law enforcement or staff as voting members (using a separate Community Resource Panel instead) and form a three-body drafting team to finalize bylaws.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Steve Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson argued the task force was community-initiated and designed for ongoing engagement alongside immediate crisis-response audits rather than delaying action for two years, and endorsed Commissioner Reckhow's Community Resource Panel compromise to keep voting seats community-only.
Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter favored county participation, though Jacobs acknowledged the board lacked consensus.
conflicts.side_b_position: Withhold county endorsement until urgent action, genuine community vetting, answers to commissioner questions, and proper respect for law enforcement and county process are addressed.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton—citing the loss of two sons to gun violence—rejected waiting two years for 'more talking and analysis,' objected that five questions she posed remained unanswered and that the city 'threw' a pre-packaged plan at the county, and argued it was not broadly community-vetted.

Vice Chair James Hill questioned why excluding the Police Chief and Sheriff from the panel was a dealbreaker given their professionalism in Durham; Council Member DeDreana Freeman agreed the rollout bypassed county committees and felt disrespectful.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow expressed concern after receiving dozens of emails opposing even law enforcement presence on the non-voting resource panel, leaving her unwilling to force a split county vote without adjusting the timeline and engaging PACs.
conflicts.resolution: No committee vote was taken on the task force; Chair Jacobs agreed to circulate an email seeking a commissioner liaison to meet with Mayor Pro Tem Johnson and a school board representative to see if bylaw revisions could resolve the impasse.

conflicts.issue: Appointment of Chair and Co-Chairs for Community-Led Task Force Bylaws
conflicts.summary: Members disagreed over whether the three governing board chairs should appoint the chair and co-chairs of a community-led task force under newly drafted bylaws, or whether task force members should select their own leadership.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow the community-led task force to elect its own chair and co-chairs rather than having the three board chairs appoint them.
side_a_arguments: Community participants have consistently asked elected officials for autonomy to lead their own work.
Top-down leadership selection risks poor community reception and reduces member ownership and buy-in.
conflicts.side_b_position: Approved bylaws assign chair appointment to the three board chairs, and any modification must be addressed by the individual boards rather than the Joint Committee.
side_b_arguments: The County Commissioners and School Board had already passed the bylaws specifying appointment by the three board chairs.
The Joint City-County Committee does not hold formal authority to amend bylaws; City Council will consider the County's recommendations when it takes up the item.
conflicts.resolution: No vote taken; Mayor Steve Schewel stated that City Council would review the County's recommendations during its own deliberations.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Newly elected Board of County Commissioners Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the December 9, 2020 Joint City-County Committee meeting alongside Durham Mayor Steve Schewel and City Council and BOCC members, honoring Mary Ann Black as the only prior African American woman to chair the BOCC. The committee received informational briefings on COVID-19 positivity (5.1%) and vaccine rollout transparency from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, year-round food security initiatives, and joint small-business relief—where $1 million in grants and $577,000 in loans had been awarded and $240,000 in Durham CARES grants were advancing ahead of the December 30 federal deadline. Officials also reviewed Hope Learning Centers funding needs for approximately 300 vulnerable students, round-two ESG COVID homeless shelter and White Flag winter operations (including whether ESG restrictions permitted hotel acquisition), and foster care / emergency rental assistance challenges before adjourning without formal votes.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Agenda Time Management, and Welcome to New BOCC Leadership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the joint committee meeting and set a 15-minute-per-report schedule to adjourn on time. Mayor Steve Schewel congratulated Chair Howerton and the newly seated county commissioners, and Howerton reflected on serving as only the second African American female BOCC chair after Mary Ann Black.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update and Vaccine Rollout Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported a 5.1% lab positivity rate and noted that outreach with El Centro Hispano, LATIN-19, and Spanish-language radio had reduced Latinx cases from 78% of new infections in early summer, while inequities persisted. Answering Council Member Johnson, Jenkins described surveys of public health, EMS, police, and fire staff for vaccine readiness and plans for community town halls on vaccine transparency.

agenda_items.title: Food Security and Eat and See Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presenter Donna reviewed partnerships with farmers markets, PPE and volunteer support for food pantries, the county-funded year-round Food Security Coordinator position, and adjustments to Eat and See family meal delivery. Chair Howerton noted that food insecurity was also an NCACC presidential priority she planned to bring forward via resolution.

agenda_items.title: Small Business Grant and Loan Fund & Durham CARES Grants Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Office of Economic and Workforce Development Director Andre Pettigrew reported that the joint $1 million small business grant program was fully awarded and the $2 million long-term (9-year, 3% interest) loan fund had lent $577,000 to 25 businesses, leaving ~$1.2 million available. He also outlined the new Durham CARES Small Business Grant program ($240,000 already awarded by the City, with County action pending before the December 30 CARES Act deadline) and addressed duplication-of-benefits tracking.

agenda_items.title: Hope Learning Centers and Digital Equity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Megan and Dr. Harding presented an update on Hope Learning Centers serving roughly 300 vulnerable students with digital equity and remote-learning support. Commissioners noted the ongoing funding gap as initial funds expire and scheduled deeper review at the upcoming BOCC meeting.

agenda_items.title: ESG COVID Funds, Homeless Shelter Operations, and White Flag Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the committee on Round 1 ESG COVID funds supporting Urban Ministries at Liberty Street and Carolina Duke Inn, over $2 million in Round 2 city ESG funds, a White Flag winter shelter program targeted for January 1, and $783,633 in competitive state ESG funds due January 22. Responding to Mayor Schewel on using ESG money to purchase a hotel instead of paying high nightly room rates, staff explained that federal ESG strings require a purchased hotel to operate solely as an emergency shelter for 3 to 10 years without covering ongoing operating costs.

agenda_items.title: Housing, Emergency Assistance, Child Welfare, and Diversion Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Department of Social Services and county staff reviewed high-volume emergency housing assistance applications, public-private partnership planning, challenges placing COVID-positive children in foster care, and diversion programs.

agenda_items.title: HB2 Discussion and Next Joint Meeting Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton reported contacting Kevin Leonard at the NCACC regarding HB2 so city and county positions stay coordinated, announced the next joint committee meeting for February 9 at 9:00 a.m., and adjourned the session.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee - Virtual Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Steve Schewel, the October 13, 2020 virtual Joint City-County Committee meeting opened with roll-call approvals of the draft minutes (amended on a correction from Council Member DeDreana Freeman) and the 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting schedule, both passing without recorded opposition. Presenters Dr. Darity, Dr. Omar Ali, and student researchers Nicholas and Baiyi (transcribed as 'by E'/'payee') shared research on redlining, gentrification, and racial home-value disparities in Durham, estimating approximately $98,000 to $100,000 in lost appreciation per home in Black census tracts since 1940 ($70 million total). The committee also received updates on pandemic-era eviction filings and overburdened rental assistance programs, small business grant and restaurant ventilation strategies alongside the Back on the Bull campaign, and partner-operated HOPE Learning Centers. In a closing non-voting policy debate over task force bylaws, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and Council Member DeDreana Freeman argued that the community-led group should elect its own chair and co-chairs rather than accept top-down appointments by the three board chairs, while Mayor Schewel maintained that formal bylaw changes rested with the individual boards rather than the Joint Committee.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Draft Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member DeDreana Freeman offered a correction to the draft minutes specifying that certain entities were being paid as for-profit businesses. Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved to approve the minutes with Freeman's correction, seconded by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow. A roll-call vote began with Mayor Steve Schewel voting Aye before the remainder of the roll call was omitted in a digest gap, after which the committee moved to the next item.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Roll Call; remainder truncated in digest)

agenda_items.title: Approval of Joint City-County 2021 Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel introduced the proposed 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting schedule included in the agenda packet. Council Member DeDreana Freeman moved approval and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded. The Clerk initiated a roll-call vote capturing Mayor Pro Tempore Jillian Johnson's Aye vote before a digest gap omitted the remaining roll call.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed (Roll Call; remainder truncated in digest)

agenda_items.title: Research Presentation on Redlining, Gentrification, and Racial Home-Value Disparities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Researchers Dr. Darity, Dr. Omar Ali, and student researchers Nicholas and Baiyi (transcribed as 'by E'/'payee') presented findings on how rising property values in Black neighborhoods correlate with the displacement of Black residents and widen the racial wealth gap. Using a counterfactual from 1940 to 2016, they estimated that Black census tracts experienced roughly $98,000 to $100,000 in lost appreciation per home, totaling around $70 million, and discussed national Brookings comparisons and potential future tracking of community land trust properties. Council Member DeDreana Freeman underscored that new public infrastructure such as streets and parks drives market-led gentrification unless racial equity is intentionally addressed.

agenda_items.title: Report on Eviction Diversion, Rental Assistance, and Vulnerable Resident Support
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The committee received a report on eviction trends and rental assistance during the COVID-19 pandemic after confirming that two registered public attendees did not wish to speak at that time. Presenters reviewed federal CARES Act eviction restrictions on subsidized and federally backed properties, Durham County Sheriff filing data compiled by DataWorks, and the fact that the Durham Housing Authority had paused non-payment filings. Although filings remained roughly half of typical annual volume due to court closures and legal protections, presenter Gilbert warned that unpaid rent vastly exceeded available federal and state assistance.

agenda_items.title: Small Business Relief, Indoor Airflow Mitigation, and Back on the Bull Campaign
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a truncated middle portion of the transcript, discussion focused on expanding small business grants and loans—including potential private-sector and Duke University contributions—and addressing airborne COVID-19 transmission risks in indoor restaurants ahead of winter. Participants discussed low-cost ventilation measures such as window box fans for negative pressure, MERV 13 air filters, outdoor dining, and a proposed Risk Mitigation Fund, while questioning whether modest HVAC upgrades alone would draw diners indoors. Staff also reviewed Back on the Bull communications, confirming to Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton that bilingual inserts were being mailed to households in monthly water bills.

agenda_items.title: HOPE Learning Centers Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A brief update on the HOPE Learning Centers noted that individual community partners—including Student U, the YMCA, Katie's Corner, and Durham Public Schools—each manage their own sites. Families seeking information across all available learning center options were encouraged to contact the DPS Foundation as a central coordination point.

agenda_items.title: Bylaws and Chair Appointment Process for Community-Led Task Force / Race Equity Commission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned the adopted bylaws assigning the appointment of the task force's chair and co-chairs to the chairs of the City Council, County Commissioners, and School Board, arguing that a community-led initiative should choose its own leaders. Council Member DeDreana Freeman supported shifting away from top-down appointments to strengthen community buy-in and suggested coordinating a single countywide Race Equity Commission rather than separate city and county bodies. Mayor Steve Schewel noted that the County and School Board had already approved the bylaws, that the Joint Committee had no formal authority to alter them, and that City Council would consider the County's recommendations separately.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting Aug 11, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 11, 2020 Joint City-County Committee virtual meeting alongside Durham Mayor Steve Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Vice Chair James Hill, Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Ellen W. Reckhow, and alternate Commissioner Heidi Carter. The committee opened with an intense policy clash over the proposed Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, as Mayor Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Johnson pressed for county participation and a three-body drafting group while Commissioner Howerton strongly opposed a two-year study lacking community vetting and Vice Chair Hill questioned excluding law enforcement from membership (with Commissioner Reckhow noting intense community pushback even to a non-voting resource panel). Once a quorum formed, the committee voted unanimously (3-0 BOCC committee; 6-0 combined) to approve the amended May 12 minutes, then received joint updates on the Small Business Recovery Fund (196 grants and $1.28 million in loans/grants across 211 businesses), the Family Justice Center's $85,508 upfit request for the former DCB building, the $1 million City-County eviction diversion partnership, feeding and homelessness programs, and the county's 4% Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program.

agenda_items.title: Technical Setup and Discussion of Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While awaiting a City quorum, Chair Jacobs reported that the BOCC remained deadlocked on the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force despite revised bylaws creating a Community Resource Panel for law enforcement and county directors. Mayor Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Johnson urged forming a three-body drafting team and proceeding regardless, while Commissioner Howerton condemned waiting two years amid gun violence and lacking answers to her five questions, Vice Chair Hill questioned excluding law enforcement, Council Member Freeman criticized the non-collaborative rollout, and Commissioner Reckhow suggested reviewing the two-year timeline and PAC engagement.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 12, 2020 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon Council Member DeDreana Freeman joining to establish a quorum, Commissioner Reckhow requested correcting the May 12 minutes where she had been mislabeled 'Council Member Reckhow.' Both delegations unanimously approved the corrected minutes by voice vote (3-0 BOCC committee; 6-0 combined).

agenda_items.title: Small Business Recovery Fund Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Economic Development staff Brian Smith and Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick reported on the $3 million joint City-County-Duke fund launched June 18, detailing 196 grants and loans across 211 small businesses in Round 1 and a July 28 Round 2 reopening. Officials discussed improvements to broaden eligibility and accelerate disbursements.

agenda_items.title: Family Justice Center (Former DCB Building) Upfit Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Crisis Response Center leaders Kent Wallace-Meigs and Liz Herron, joined by Deputy Engineering Director Perry Mands, outlined co-located survivor services for the Family Justice Center in the county-owned former DCB building (valued at $1.2M building / $2M+ site). DCRC reported covering $73,604 in IT/security costs via a Governor's Crime Commission grant expiring at the end of September and requested $85,508 jointly from the City and County for interior upfits.

agenda_items.title: City-County Emergency Rental Assistance and Eviction Diversion Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and DSS Assistant Director Janine Gordon presented the joint eviction diversion program pairing over $1 million in City CDBG-CV funds (with zero administrative fee holdback) and $500,000 in City legal aid funds with DSS program administration. Eligible city residents under 80% AMI with COVID-19 income loss can enter via either DSS or Legal Aid for up to three continuous months and $6,000 maximum paid directly to landlords and utilities.

agenda_items.title: City-County Feeding and Homeless Programs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt and City Homeless Systems Manager Colin Davis briefed the committee on Durham Feast (>500,000 meals through July 31), COVID-positive family deliveries, senior/Latinx contracts, 611+ volunteers, the newly established county food security coordinator position, and non-congregate shelter coordination ahead of HUD Round 2 consolidated plan amendments.

agenda_items.title: Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Dwane Brinson presented the county's newly approved Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Repayment Plan capping property tax payments at 4% of income for homeowners under age 65 earning <=30% AMI with 10+ years of ownership, alongside the new online Property Tax Assistance Evaluator, Community Land Trust tax options, and home-repair concepts. Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and Council Member Freeman welcomed the program—asking Brinson to present to City Council and model 60% AMI and 2% scenarios—while commissioners noted they were exploring private donation check-offs and nonprofit financial counseling.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 12, 2020 Joint City-County Committee Minutes (as Corrected)
votes.notes: BOCC committee voting members Howerton, Reckhow, and Jacobs voted Aye (3-0; alternate Heidi Carter also voiced Aye, and City Council members DeDreana Freeman, Steve Schewel, and Jillian Johnson voted Aye for a combined 6-0 committee approval).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the May 12, 2020 minutes after correcting a reference that misidentified Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow as a Council Member.

meetings.title: Virtual Joint City-County Committee Meeting May 12, 2020 (Live Stream)
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Steve Schewel on May 12, 2020, the Virtual Joint City-County Committee convened Durham City Council members, Durham County Commissioners, and invited Durham Public Schools Board of Education members for a joint COVID-19 response briefing. In its lone formal action, voting committee members approved the March 10, 2020 minutes by a 3-0 roll-call majority (Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson alongside Commissioners Jacobs and Hill, while DeDreana Freeman had audio difficulty and Commissioner Reckhow joined later with minor corrections). Officials heard updates from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins (including 30% of deaths among African American residents and four outbreak facilities), homeless isolation motel operations (zero COVID-19 cases), emergency feeding for DPS students and seniors amid 40.7% statewide food insecurity, the Recovery and Renewal Task Force (with DeDreana Freeman urging a community-focused counterpart alongside business recovery), eviction diversion and $500,000 in CDBG rental assistance, DPS's 13,336-device digital divide needs, and a proposed $50,000 joint Cover Durham mask initiative ($20k County, $20k City, $10k Schools).

agenda_items.title: Welcome to School Board Members and Approval of March 10, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Steve Schewel welcomed City Council, County Commissioners, and Durham Public Schools Board members to the joint COVID-19 review session and corrected Jillian Johnson's name spelling in the March 10 minutes. On a motion by Commissioner Jacobs and second by Commissioner Hill, a majority of voting committee members (Jillian Johnson, Commissioner Jacobs, and Commissioner Hill) approved the minutes 3-0 while DeDreana Freeman experienced audio trouble and Commissioner Reckhow later supplied two minor wording corrections.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County COVID-19 Public Health Update (Director Rod Jenkins)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported outbreak breakdowns (70% close contacts, 17% community spread, 12% travel, ~14% healthcare workers), four outbreak facilities supported alongside Duke University Medical Center, and ongoing enforcement of Durham's face-covering order. Officials questioned the stark racial disparity showing African Americans accounting for 30% of COVID-19 deaths and asked what targeted interventions were underway.

agenda_items.title: Homeless Isolation Hotel and Emergency Feeding Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Colin reported zero COVID-19 cases among homeless residents sheltered in the county-city isolation motel. Donna Rewalt then briefed officials on emergency feeding for DPS students, families, and seniors, citing a late-March 2020 survey showing 40.7% statewide food insecurity and launching an accelerated End Hunger Durham GIS food-access map.

agenda_items.title: Recovery and Renewal Task Force and Senior Care Protections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presenters outlined Recovery and Renewal Task Force support for restaurants and places of worship while coordinating with DPS and universities. DeDreana Freeman urged establishing a dedicated community-focused task force rather than squeezing community needs into a business-oriented task force, and another official urged studying long-term care best practices to protect seniors.

agenda_items.title: Eviction Diversion, Emergency Rental Assistance, and DPS Digital Divide
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported eviction diversion funding was nearly depleted ($136,725 of $180,000 spent by February 28 with 913 March filings) and outlined a $500,000 CDBG rental assistance program, with DeDreana Freeman underscoring food and housing stability. DPS staff then estimated 13,336 devices and hotspots needed for remote learning equity, prompting school board member Natalie Beyer and commissioners to call for long-term community-wide broadband funding using CARES Act and public-private partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Cover Durham Joint Mask Funding Request ($50,000) and Minute Corrections
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After accepting Commissioner Reckhow's two minor corrections to the March 10 minutes, Commissioners Reckhow and Howerton proposed a $50,000 joint Cover Durham mask distribution initiative (15,000 masks via Community Health Coalition funded $20,000 by the County, $20,000 by the City, and $10,000 by DPS) out of unspent travel and meeting funds. Mayor Steve Schewel agreed to poll City Council on unspent travel funds before adjourning at 12:03 p.m.

votes.notes: Joint City-County Committee vote: ayes lists seated City Council member from SEATED_BOARD_ROSTER who voted Aye (Jillian Johnson). meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Mayor Steve Schewel under a strict 11:00 a.m. adjournment deadline, the January 14, 2020 Joint City-County Committee deferred minutes approval at the outset due to an initial lack of quorum and focused on property tax relief and youth workforce readiness. City and County legal counsel alongside Durham County Tax Administrator Duane Brinson (ASR spelling) outlined North Carolina statutory property tax exemptions, constitutional limits prohibiting direct tax rebates, and legal parameters for restricting any local assistance program to low-income homeowners via a nonprofit administrator. By unanimous voice vote (including an amendment from Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow to consider family financial counseling), the committee directed City and County administrations to return by March with program alternatives for the upcoming budget cycle. Finally, Made in Durham Executive Director Casey Steinbacher and Durham Literacy Center Executive Director Lizzie presented the six-month interim report on opportunity youth, highlighting free youth bus pass access while flagging transit gaps to Treyburn jobs and the challenge of securing backbone funding.

agenda_items.title: Property Tax Relief Update and Direction to Administrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A Durham City Attorney's Office representative, Deputy County Attorney Brian Wardell (transcribed 'Ward Dell'), and Durham County Tax Administrator Duane Brinson reviewed the three existing North Carolina statutory property tax exemptions, property revaluation pressures on homeowners, and an upcoming online eligibility tool for public libraries and community centers. Attorneys explained that state statutes and the Constitution prohibit direct tax rebates and require any local relief program—potentially administered by a nonprofit—to serve low-income households (such as 30%–50% AMI) rather than moderate-income residents, while noting the City Manager's plan to shift toward outreach on existing exemptions. Following comments from Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the committee voted unanimously to direct staff to return by March with program alternatives incorporating financial counseling.

agenda_items.title: Made in Durham Six-Month Interim Report and Opportunity Youth Collaboration
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Made in Durham Executive Director Casey Steinbacher and Durham Literacy Center Executive Director Lizzie reported on opportunity youth outcomes, noting that roughly 60% of Durham youth were on track while 25% were behind and 15% of older youth were disconnected. They highlighted collaborative wraparound supports—including GoTriangle/GoDurham youth bus passes up to age 18 distributed through nonprofit agencies and housing assistance from the Life Skills Foundation—that helped Durham Futures students earn high school diplomas and enter Durham Tech. In post-presentation discussion ahead of budget season, members lamented that bus routes still fail to reach advanced manufacturing jobs in Treyburn even for Durham Tech Promise scholars, while Steinbacher cited the lack of a unified countywide youth master plan and difficulty securing corporate or philanthropic funding for backbone coordination.

votes.item_title: Direct City and County Administrations to Develop Property Tax Relief Program Alternatives
votes.notes: Chair Steve Schewel put the proposal forward for a show of hands and voice vote with Commissioner Reckhow's correction; no formal mover or seconder was named in the transcript. The seven listed members are those confirmed present or speaking in the transcript digest, and the Chair declared the motion passed unanimously.
